operative_text.controlling:
2.17(1)  If the Court appoints a lawyer as the litigation
representative for an individual referred to in rule 2.11(a) to (d), the
Court may direct that the costs incurred in performing the duties of
the litigation representative be borne by
(a) the parties or by one or more of them, or
(b) any fund in Court in which the individual for whom the
litigation representative is appointed has an interest.
(2)  The Court may give any other direction for repayment of costs
or for an advance payment of costs as the circumstances require.

BOOK_C.title: Lawyer appointed as litigation representative

commentary.text: Rule 2.17(1) provides that the court may require the defendant to pay the costs of a litigation representative for a child. This does not limit the court’s ability to appoint someone other than the Public Trustee as a child’s litigation representative, at the Public Trustee’s cost, or to require the Public Trustee to pay the reasonable costs of a child’s litigation representative where it is not appropriate for the Public Trustee to act as litigation representative. Rules 2.17(2) and 2.21 permits a court-appointed litigation representative to apply for advance costs. C. (L.) v. Alberta (Metis Settlements Child & Family Services Region 10), [2011] A.J. No. 84, 2011 ABQB 42 at paras. 61-62 (Alta. Q.B.); , [2013] A.J. No.

citations.style_of_cause: C. (L.) v. Alberta (Metis Settlements Child & Family Services Region 10), [2011] A.J. No. 84

commentary.review_flag: useful and unique: defendant may be ordered to pay a child's litigation representative's costs; Public Trustee cost options; 2.17(2) and 2.21 allow advance costs (C.(L.) 2011 ABQB 42 paras 61-62). Ends with a cut-off second citation ('[2013] A.J. No.'). Read with the official text (4th pass): 2.17(1) applies only when the Court appoints a LAWYER as litigation representative for an individual in 2.11(a)-(d), and lets costs be borne by 'the parties or ... one or more of them' or a fund in Court - Book C's 'the defendant' is one instance of that.
